contract_units.what: the admission / identification of a new authority and the record of its identity and profile as the delta input pair, exercised on the already-admitted `openssl-3.6.3-historical` versus `openssl-3.6.4-production` (`forensics/authorities/AUTHORITIES.json`, the two `SOURCE_MANIFEST.{3.6.3,3.6.4}.json` files)

the added / removed / changed obligation delta between the two authorities, computed across the atlas planes the procedure names -- exports, provider registration rows and prerequisite units -- mechanically from committed artefacts (the differential `forensics/atlas/differential/openssl-3.6.3-historical-vs-openssl-3.6.4-production.json` and the per-authority atlases), never hand-listed

the disposition of every delta row (`implemented` / `deferred` / `not-in-profile` / `boundary`), requiring zero unexplained, so a newly discovered un-dispositioned delta row is a `fail` rather than a silent addition
the derivation of which courts a delta touches, recorded with the selection derivation, so the selected courts are re-run or re-derived and a delta reaches exactly the courts its obligations do

the register that records the explicit non-claims -- OpenSSL 4.x is a new compatibility profile and a 3.x receipt is never silently reinterpreted as evidence for 4, only the exercised delta is claimed, and unknown stays unknown -- and that fails the stratum if a recorded boundary drifts from its evidence

body.note: `open` is the only list that blocks this stratum, and its count is over the maintenance delta contract units rather than exported symbols, so the `implemented` and `open` *export* lists are empty by measurement and `open_in_this_stratum` is the live count. Phase 21 owns no provider registration row and no export: it activates no provider and adds no library surface, because it computes the delta between two authorities that are already admitted. Its five contract units are the maintenance delta contract docs/PHASE-21-SUBPHASES.md section 1 names -- the authority admission, the atlas delta, the delta disposition, the affected-court selection and the maintenance-boundary register -- and at activation all five are open, so this stratum's working set is exactly its five contract units. Nothing here is a version-universality claim: a passing delta court measures the movement between the two authorities it names and nothing beyond them, because OpenSSL 4.x is a new compatibility profile and a 3.x receipt is never silently reinterpreted as evidence for 4 (docs/RELEASE_GATES.md section 8, docs/NON_CLAIMS.md section 3). Only the exercised delta is claimed, and unknown stays unknown: a delta row the courts cannot disposition is `UNKNOWN`, a research result rather than a resting state (docs/PARITY_MODEL.md section 1). A 3.6.3 behaviour that corresponds to an upstream security fix is not reintroduced (docs/SECURITY_DIVERGENCE_POLICY.md section 1). Each contract unit records its two axes separately: `measurement_state` says the instrument completed, and `property_status`/`findings` say what is claimed about a delta property. The `delta-disposition` unit's property is `NOT_CLAIMED` with every un-dispositioned change named as a finding, so a passing `RT-DELTA-DISPOSITION` is an instrument plus a disposition record and must never be read as 'the delta is implemented'.
body.rule: this stratum's working set is not a set of exported symbols: Phase 21 owns no export, no provider registration row and no prerequisite deferral, so its working set is exactly the maintenance delta contract units docs/PHASE-21-SUBPHASES.md names, each measured by the Phase-21 courts registry. Every row is read from those atlases; the ledger types none of them, and `main` fails closed if the ownership atlas assigns this stratum an export, the provider census assigns it a row, or the prerequisite plane assigns it a deferral or unit
